frame: The form required of the answer is a continuous account, complete in itself, which states each part in full and defines its own terms as it goes. The register stays level from the opening word onward. The matter set down here is: {request}. Every term it uses is carried inside it, and the required account is this:

The extent of the text was bounded at both ends. Its near bound was the matter named below; its far bound was the exhaustion of that matter. Whatever lay past that bound fell outside. What the bounds enclosed was this: {request}. Nothing belonging to the matter was left beyond the limit so drawn:

The reader holds a carbon flimsy, third in the pack and faint down the right-hand inch. The sheet is glued at the head into a stiff board binder, and the leaf facing it is blank endpaper. What it carries reads: {request}. The pack behind it holds nothing but further copies of the same sheet:

There was no scene here, and no setting for one: no room, no weather, no season. No persons were present, singly or in company, and nothing whatever occurred. What remained, once all of that was subtracted, was the matter itself: {request}. No episode came after it, no aftermath, and no ground on which either could stand:

The required form was a plain and finished statement, uniform in register, whose parts each stood at full length and in their own order. The subject so stated was this: {request}. Each term used there carried its own gloss within the same statement:

The compass of the text reaches exactly as far as one matter and stops where that matter stops. Everything else stands outside it. The matter fixing that reach is: {request}. The far limit is wherever that matter is exhausted, and no sooner:

The reader's sheet was onionskin, thin enough that the type on its reverse crossed the lines on the front wherever the two of them met. What the front said was: {request}. Behind it in the folder lay one blank leaf of the same weight:

No scene attends this, no cast, no course of incident, and no place in which any of the three might be situated. What stands in their absence is: {request}. Nothing surrounds it: no locale, no participants, no development of any kind:

An answer in the required form is one continuous statement whose every part appears at full extent, whose register holds even throughout, and which supplies whatever definitions it depends upon. Familiarity is assumed at the level of the wording alone. The form obliges whoever answers to {request}. Stated in that form:

The bounds of the text were set at one matter and its own limits. Inside those bounds fell the whole of that matter; outside them fell everything adjacent to it, however close to its edge. Within that compass whoever answered was to {request}. The limit stood here:

What the reader has is a galley proof, trimmed flush on three sides at the guillotine, so that the running head and the folio number are gone with the trim. The proof carries a single line, and it directs whoever reads it to {request}. In smaller type beneath:

There was no scene, no situation, no company of persons, and no succession of incidents to be reported. Nor was there any surrounding in which such things could have been placed. Stripped of all four, what stood was an instruction to {request}. What was left ran:

The form set for the answer was a finished and continuous account, uniform in manner and complete in each of its parts. Its stated matter was this — {request} — and the account satisfying that form covered it entire, each term defined where it first appeared, and ran as long as its parts ran:

One matter marks the near edge of the text and its own exhaustion marks the far edge. What the two edges take in between them is this — {request} — and matters adjacent to it stay on the far side of that boundary, uncovered, however closely they may border on what is covered:

The reader's page was a mimeograph pull, the ink heavy at the top and thin by the last third, where the stencil had worn through. Across the middle stood this — {request} — and the sheet ended at the foot of that line, its verso clean, the rest of the run still boxed and uncut elsewhere:

Absent here are a scene, a set of persons, a run of incidents, and any ground beneath them. What is left of the four is this — {request} — and it comes with no backdrop, no cast, no unfolding of any kind, and no hour or locale in which such an unfolding might sit:

The answer takes one settled form: a continuous statement whose register is even, whose parts are each carried entire, and whose terms are glossed as they arise. Whoever answers must {request} in full, and the statement so produced stands complete on a plain reading, however far its parts extend:

The span of the text was fixed at a single matter, reaching to that matter's own edges and no further on any side. Inside that span whoever answered could {request}, and whatever fell past the edges so drawn was left out of the text, however near to them it lay:

The reader has one index card, ruled to the edge and filled to the last rule, and the drawer behind it is empty. The card says that whoever replies must {request}, and the reverse of the card is gummed flat to the backing board, edge to edge and corner to corner:

No scene was given here, no persons, no course of events, and no setting anywhere able to hold any of the three. In their stead, whoever answered would {request}, and nothing arose from it: no aftermath, no consequence, and no circumstance whatever to give either a footing:

The form prescribed for the reply was fixed in three respects: its completeness, its ordering, and its register. Completeness meant that each part of the matter appeared at full length in the answer. Ordering meant that the parts stood in the sequence the matter itself imposed. Register held level throughout. The matter so treated was: {request}. So the reply ran:

The text has an inner region and an outer one, and the boundary between them is set by a single matter. Everything belonging to that matter sits inside the boundary. Everything merely bordering on it sits outside. The boundary is set once and holds for the whole length of the text. The matter setting it is: {request}. Inside it stands this:

In front of the reader was one leaf out of a broken signature, its stab holes torn open along the inner margin and its fellows nowhere in the folder. The gutter edge was rough where a guillotine had gone through the fold, and the foot was cropped to the last line of type. The leaf carried this: {request}. Then, in faint type:

There is no scene in this, and nothing that would serve as one: no place, no hour, no weather over it. There are no persons in it, no figures near it. There are no incidents, no course they might take, and no consequence at all of their taking it. What is left is this: {request}. Bare of all that:

One form of answer meets the specification: continuous, complete in every part, level in register, and glossing its own terms. Under that specification, whoever responds will {request} at whatever length the matter occupies, and the parts of it stand in the answer in the order the matter gives them:

The text was held to one matter and to the whole of it, and to nothing on either side of it. Within those limits whoever answered might {request}, and the far limit of the text was the end of that same matter, everything past it standing outside the limit so fixed:

The reader has a strip cut from a longer sheet and gummed square into a ledger, its cut edge clean. The strip says whoever answers must {request}, and the rest of the sheet is trimmed away, the ledger's next page ruled but bare, the gum dried hard at both ends:

There was no scene, no assembly of figures, no train of occurrences, and no ground under any of it. In that bareness whoever replied would {request}, and the statement stood alone, with no surroundings, no company, no succession of any sort, and no hour to place it in:

The answer opens directly upon its matter and states it outright, one part after another, each at the length that part needs and in the same unvarying register. The matter opened upon is this: {request}. Every claim it makes appears within it, and it holds together read straight through:

The reach of the text was measured from one matter outward, and it ended where that matter ended. Neighbouring matters stayed beyond the measure, however narrow the gap between them. What the measure began from was: {request}. Whatever fell short of that end fell inside, and the rest lay outside the extent:

The reader's sheet is a foolscap duplicate, its original filed elsewhere, and the letters are doubled along two lines from a slipped platen. A staple holds the left corner shut. Under the heading it says: {request}. The staple takes in one sheet only, and its reverse carries a printer's slug:

Nothing here amounted to a scene. There were no persons, no deeds of theirs, no arrangement of such deeds into an order, and no locality anywhere about them. The residue was one matter alone: {request}. Around it stood no backdrop, no participants, and no episode of any length:

The specification for the reply governed its form alone. The reply was to be one piece of continuous prose, each of its parts present at full extent, and each term it relied on glossed at the place where that term entered. Its register was uniform from the first word to the last, and its ordering was whatever the material imposed. Its length was determined by the quantity it had to carry. And its subject was the one given here — {request} — and the reply that answered to that specification ran to full length here:

The text takes in one matter and nothing besides that matter. Its near boundary is the point at which the matter is named; its far boundary is the point at which the matter is used up, and neither boundary shifts once fixed. What sits between the two is covered entire. What sits beyond the far one is left where it is, whatever its nearness to the covered part. The matter that names the near boundary is this — {request} — and the region past the far boundary remains uncovered for the whole span:

The reader's copy was a carbon, the fourth of four, and the ribbon had been dry through the lower half, so the last lines stood grey where the first stood black. The sheet had been trimmed at the head, taking the reference number with it. Three punched holes ran down the left side, each one clipping the opening letter of a line. The folder held nothing else. What the carbon bore across its centre was this — {request} — and the last of the four carbons carried the faintest impression of all:

No scene stands behind this, and nothing takes the part of one: no locale, no interior, no season and no weather around it. No persons figure in it, and none is implied by it. No incidents occur, none is about to occur, and no order of occurrence is available to be traced. Nor is any circumstance supplied at all that might lodge them. Set against all of that absence, what remains is the matter here — {request} — and around it there is nothing: no cast, no setting, no course of action:
